data.title: Thailand, UNESCO Join Forces at AFE 2026 for Equitable Education
data.description: 23 October 2026 – The Equitable Education Fund (EEF) Thailand and the UNESCO Regional Office in Bangkok and Office for UN Coordination for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCO Bangkok), under the Equitable Education Alliance (EEA) framework, co-organised the 4th International Conference on Equitable Education , also known as the All for Education Conference 2026 (AFE 2026), from 23–24 October 2026 at IMPACT Forum, Nonthaburi, Thailand. Under the theme “Designing Tomorrow’s Equity: Equitable Solutions for Out-of-School Children and Youth by 2030 and Beyond,” the Conference focused on developing solutions for out-of-school children and youth to make education systems more equitable, inclusive, and flexible.

data.title: AI-generated ad blitz distorts US midterms
data.description: WASHINGTON - The video looks hyper-real, depicting a US Senate candidate laughing at cards that read "Death to America" and "Celebrate 9/11". But it is part of a multimillion-dollar blitz of AI-generated political ads ahead of the midterm elections.

data.title: Rain, runoff, rocks and mud slam Phuket
data.description: PHUKET - Persistent rain caused runoff that washed big rocks and mud into communities and tourist venues in this southern island province early Monday morning.

data.title: China's Communist Party elite gather for governance talks
data.description: BEIJING - China's President Xi Jinping and other top leaders meet in Beijing on Monday at a key gathering watched closely for clues as to the country's direction and future leadership.

data.title: Have a family-frightening  Halloween at The Mall Bangkapi
data.description: Thrill-seekers are invited to embark on a journey through an extraordinary world of mystery during "The Ghost Halloween #3" which is running at The Mall Lifestore Bangkapi, Lat Phrao Road, until Nov 8.

data.title: Malaysia's Padu wraps World Film Series
data.description: The 2026 Contemporary World Film Series will conclude with a screening of Padu from Malaysia, at TK Park, 8th floor of CentralWorld, Ratchadamri Road, on Saturday at 4pm.

data.title: 'I am here': Opposition leader Machado returns to Venezuela
data.description: GUACARA (VENEZUELA) - Maria Corina Machado, Venezuela's opposition leader and a Nobel Peace Prize winner, returned home on Sunday after nearly a year in exile, in a direct challenge to the US-backed interim government.

data.title: Flights resume at Riyadh airport as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
data.description: RIYADH (SAUDI ARABIA) - Flights resumed at Riyadh's international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen's Houthis targeted the country with strikes.

data.title: Aleksandar Vucic: Serbia's veteran ruler felled by student-led movement
data.description: BELGRADE - The dominant force in Serbian politics for over 14 years, Aleksandar Vucic, who conceded defeat in a snap parliamentary poll on Sunday, rose from the wreckage of strongman Slobodan Milosevic's cabinet to the centre of power using his brand of populist nationalism.

data.title: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix to close on world title
data.description: AUSTIN - Kimi Antonelli moved to within striking distance of his first world championship title as he powered to an emphatic victory at the US Grand Prix in Austin on Sunday.

data.title: Mbappe double helps Real Madrid stun Barca in La Liga Clasico
data.description: BARCELONA - Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.

data.title: Tiger March passes toughest test to claim WBA Asia South title
data.description: When you look at Siriyakorn Chamjaiharn, better known as Tiger March, you see a 15-year-old kid with blonde hair whose father is a former guitarist of the prominent Thai pop-rock band Potato. Boxing might not be the first thing that comes to mind, but the youngster is already making a name for himself inside the professional ring.

data.title: Water, ways of life  converge at 'Confluent'
data.description: Miranda Housden explores water in Thai and Western mythologies for her solo exhibition at Bangkok University Gallery, running until Nov 25.

data.title: Pages of inspiration
data.description: Book lovers are invited to discover new stories, ideas and inspiration at the 31st National Book Expo, organised by the Publishers and Booksellers Association of Thailand (Pubat) under the theme "Unread Messages".

data.title: Minnows shock Buriram in Isan derby
data.description: Defending champions Buriram United suffered their first defeat of the Thai League 1 season on Saturday night, beaten 3-2 at home by northeastern rivals Sisaket United in a derby that few had seen coming.

data.title: Public 'not convinced' by welfare policies
data.description: Some 64.85% of respondents lack confidence in the Anutin Charnvirakul government's welfare provision, with others saying Thais have limited access to state benefits, a Suan Dusit Poll survey has found.

data.title: Democrats prepare lawsuit over Bangkok flood claims
data.description: The Democrat Party is preparing to sue the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and other state agencies in the Administrative Court over alleged negligence in handling floods in the capital, seeking full compensation for affected residents.

data.title: Pressure mounts over sea ruling
data.description: Thailand should endorse the 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award to protect its maritime trade interests, preserve regional peace and uphold the maritime framework Unclos, says former Philippine Supreme Court Justice Antonio Carpio.

data.title: Ex-Democrat MP slams online gambling crackdown
data.description: Former Democrat Party MP Sirichok Sopha has questioned the effectiveness of the Digital Economy and Society (DES) Ministry's crackdown on online gambling, claiming major websites remain accessible despite the blocking of nearly one million URLs.

data.title: Govt insists border  artefacts are Thai
data.description: Culture Minister Sabeeda Thaised has rejected Cambodia's demand for the return of artefacts found at Prasat Khana on the Thai-Cambodian border, insisting the items are Thai antiquities protected under Thai law.
